questions.q: Distinguish autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition with examples.
questions.a: Autotrophs make food from CO2 and water using sunlight (plants); heterotrophs depend on ready food (animals, fungi).

questions.q: How does amoeba take its food?
questions.a: It surrounds food with finger-like pseudopodia forming a food vacuole, where digestion occurs.
Drawing nourishment from another living organism (host) without killing it at once, e.g. tapeworm, cuscuta.

questions.q: Why is oxygen transport efficient in humans?
questions.a: The pigment haemoglobin carries large amounts of oxygen from lungs to tissues.

questions.q: State the path of food after swallowing.
questions.a: Food pipe (oesophagus) -> stomach -> small intestine -> large intestine; digestion and absorption mostly in the small intestine.

questions.q: Why do plants not need a circulatory system like animals?
questions.a: Each plant part is close to water and minerals carried by xylem, and phloem moves food - no pumping organ is needed.

questions.q: How is urine formed in the nephron?
questions.a: Blood is filtered in the glomerulus; the filtrate loses water, glucose and salts by reabsorption, leaving urine.

questions.q: Name two excretory products of plants useful to humans.
Why must aquatic animals excrete ammonia directly?
questions.a: Water around them dissolves and carries ammonia away instantly, so it needs no conversion to urea.
